'''Bidyendu Mohan Deb''' (born 27 September 1942) is an Indian theoretical chemist, chemical physicist and a professor at the [[Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Kolkata]] (IISER).<ref name="Visiting Professor ">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iiserkol.ac.in/people/faculty/dcs/bidyendudeb |title=Visiting Professor |date=2016 |publisher=IISER Kolkata |access-date=19 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120183948/http://www.iiserkol.ac.in/people/faculty/dcs/bidyendudeb |archive-date=20 November 2016 }}</ref> He is known for his studies in [[theoretical chemistry]] and chemical physics.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=443 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> He is part of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]], [[The World Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="TWAS fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://twas.org/member/deb-bidyendu-mohan |title=TWAS fellow |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref> [[Indian National Science Academy]]<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N87-0956 |title=Indian fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=19 November 2016 |archive-date=6 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306024140/https://www.insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N87-0956 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Deb,_Prof._Bidyendu_Mohan |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> 

In 1981, the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]] for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Bidyendu Deb was born on 27 September 1942 in [[Bengal Province, British India|Bengal province]] in [[British India]]. He obtained his Honours [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in Chemistry from the [[Presidency College, Kolkata|Presidency College]] in [[Kolkata]] (now Presidency University) and completed his [[master's degree]] in [[physical chemistry]] at the [[Rajabazar Science College]] (now the University College of Science, Technology and Agriculture).<ref name="Faculty profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iiserkol.ac.in/component/sobipro/?pid=222&sid=143:Bidyendu-Mohan-Deb-FASc-FNA-FTWAS&Itemid=0 |title=Faculty profile |date=2016 |publisher=IISER Kolkata |access-date=19 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120003345/http://www.iiserkol.ac.in/component/sobipro/?pid=222&sid=143:Bidyendu-Mohan-Deb-FASc-FNA-FTWAS&Itemid=0 |archive-date=20 November 2016 }}</ref> 

Subsequently, he joined [[Santi Ranjan Palit|S. R. Palit]] at the [[Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science]] (IACS) for a year, before moving to the [[University of Oxford]]'s [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford|Mathematical Institute]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} There, he completed a Diploma in Advanced Mathematics on a Commonwealth scholarship.{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} Continuing at Oxford, he completed his doctoral research under the supervision of [[Charles Coulson]], obtaining a [[Doctor of Philosophy|DPhil]] in mathematics.<ref name="Indian fellow" />

== Professional career ==
Deb started his early professional career in 1969 as a [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research|CSIR]] pool officer. In 1970, he moved to the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Mumbai]] (IIT Mumbai) as a faculty member.<ref name="Visiting Professor" /> In 1971, he was appointed as an assistant professor at the [[Birla Institute of Technology and Science]] in Pilani (BITS Pilani).{{Citation needed|date=May 2026}} He spent a year there before returning to IIT Mumbai, where he spent the next 12 years, serving as an assistant professor (1973–78) and as a professor (1978–84).<ref name="Faculty profile" /> 

In 1984, Deb moved to [[Panjab University]] as a professor of theoretical chemistry and taught there until his retirement in 2004. After his retirement, he took up the position of ISRO Vikram Sarabhai Research Professor at the [[S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences]] in [[Kolkata]]. Not long after in 2007, he took up the position of Adjunct/Visiting Professorship at the [[Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Kolkata|Indian Institute of Science Education and Research]] in Kolkata.{{cn|date=May 2026}}

Currently, he serves<ref name="Bidyendu Mohan Deb">{{Cite journal |last=Richa Malhotra |title=Bidyendu Mohan Deb |url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/102/02/165a.pdf |journal=Current Science |date=2016 |volume=102 |issue=2}}</ref> as an INSA Senior Scientist and Honorary Scholar-in-Residence at [[Visva-Bharati University]].<ref name="News from Panjab University">{{Cite web |url=http://www.indianewscalling.com/haryana/news/38919-news-from-punjab-university-chandigarh.aspx |title=News from Panjab University |date=26 April 2016 |publisher=India News Callin |access-date=19 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161119183102/http://www.indianewscalling.com/haryana/news/38919-news-from-punjab-university-chandigarh.aspx |archive-date=19 November 2016 }}</ref>

== Legacy ==
{{Peacock|date=May 2026|section}}
Deb's main contributions are in the field of [[theoretical chemistry]] and the [[molecular geometry]] model he developed to demonstrate the influence of [[Electronuclear force|electronuclear attractive force]] and one of the highest occupied molecular orbitals in the determination of molecular shapes.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=5 October 2016 | page=34 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> His work on the applicability of the concept of internal stresses of molecules and solids revealed their relation to the [[Density functional theory|density-functional theory]] and quantum fluid dynamics. He developed methodologies for predicting new molecules using [[quantum chemistry]] and for combining cellular automata with Thomas-Fermi-Dirac theory.<ref name="Indian fellow" />

One of the early pioneers of the electron density theory in chemistry, Deb's main focus was on developing the foundations for a possible density-based alternative quantum mechanics bypassing the Schrödinger equation and the many-electron wave-function.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Deb |first=B. M. |date=20 November 1981 |title=On the Direct Calculation of Electron Density in Many-Electron Systems |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/24086528 |journal=Current Science |volume=50 |issue=22 |pages=973–976 |jstor=24086528 |via=JSTOR}}</ref> He emphasized the general interpretative aspects of the electron density in chemistry. For both these ends, he concentrated on developing a single time-dependent equation (the Deb-Chattaraj or DC equation) for the direct calculation of [[electron density]], which is different from the usual density functional theory.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Deb |first1=B. M. |last2=Chattaraj |first2=P. K. |date=15 February 1989 |title=Density-functional and hydrodynamical approach to ion-atom collisions through a new generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation |url=https://harvest.aps.org/v2/journals/articles/10.1103/PhysRevA.39.1696/fulltext |journal=Physical Review A |volume=39 |issue=4 |pages=1696–1713 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.39.1696 |pmid=9901424 |bibcode=1989PhRvA..39.1696D |via=APS}}</ref> 

His research have been published in peer-reviewed academic journals<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Deb=3ABidyendu_Mohan=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and he has authored two books, ''The Force Concept in Chemistry''<ref name="Deb1981">{{cite book|author=B. M. Deb|title=The Force concept in chemistry|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MOqFAAAAIAAJ|date=February 1981|publisher=Van Nostrand Reinhold|isbn=978-0-442-26106-1}}</ref> and ''The Single-Particle Density in Physics and Chemistry''.<ref name="MarchDeb1987">{{cite book|author1=Norman Henry March|author2=B. M. Deb|title=The single-particle density in physics and chemistry|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2Gd9AAAAIAAJ|year=1987|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=978-0-12-470518-0}}</ref> He has also written about [[holistic education]] as well as on [[Satyajit Ray]], one of the pioneers of modern Indian cinema.<ref name="GhoshChattaraj2016">{{cite book|author1=Swapan Kumar Ghosh|author2=Pratim Kumar Chattaraj|title=Concepts and Methods in Modern Theoretical Chemistry: Electronic Structure and Reactivity|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0edMBgAAQBAJ&pg=PR14|date=19 April 2016|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4665-0531-5|pages=14–}}</ref> He was also involved with curriculum designing programs and seminars<ref name="9th CRSI-RSC Symposium">{{Cite web |url=http://crsi2015.ncl.res.in/StaticPages/Resources/programme.pdf |title=9th CRSI-RSC Symposium |date=2016 |publisher=National Chemical Laboratory |access-date=19 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120003411/http://crsi2015.ncl.res.in/StaticPages/Resources/programme.pdf |archive-date=20 November 2016 }}</ref> and has been associated with science journals as a member of their editorial boards.<ref name="Indian fellow" /><ref name="International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry ">{{Cite web |url=https://www.iupac.org/publications/pac/2009/pdf/8101x00c3.pdf |title=International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry  |date=2016 |publisher=International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry }}</ref>

In 2015, he published the book "The peacock in splendour: Science, literature and arts in ancient and medieval India" which focuses on [[Indology]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Deb |first=B. M. |title=The peacock in splendour: science, literature and art in ancient and medieval India |date=2015 |publisher=Visva Bharati |others=Visva-Bharati |isbn=978-81-7522-452-0 |location=Kolkata}}</ref>
== Awards and honors ==
{{Create list|date=May 2026|section}}

The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded Deb the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1981.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | access-date=7 November 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=12 September 2012 }}</ref> [[File:B M Deb SS Bhatnagar Prize 1981.jpg|thumb|B M Deb SS Bhatnagar Prize 1981]] A guest scholar of the [[Kyoto University]] in 1989 and an honorary professor of the [[Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research]] from 1992 to 2004, he received the Sir C. V. Raman Award in Physical Sciences of the [[University Grants Commission of India]] in 1988, Biennial Professor S. R. Palit Memorial Award of the [[Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science]] in 1995 and the [[Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry|FICCI]] Award in Physical Sciences in 1996.<ref name="Faculty profile" /> He is also a recipient of the Silver Medal (2000) and the Gold Medal (2015) of the [[Chemical Research Society of India]].<ref name="Visiting Professor " /> The list of award orations he has delivered include Linus Pauling Memorial Lecture of [[Mahatma Gandhi University, Kerala|Mahatma Gandhi University]] (1996), Professor Sadhan Basu Memorial Lecture of the Indian National Science Academy (1999),<ref name="Professor Sadhan Basu Memorial Lecture">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#sadhan |title=Professor Sadhan Basu Memorial Lecture |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=19 November 2016 |archive-date=16 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#sadhan }}</ref> Mitra Memorial Lecture of [[Delhi University]] (2000),<ref name="Mitra Memorial Lecture">{{Cite web |url=http://people.du.ac.in/~rkant/MitraMemorial.html |title=Mitra Memorial Lecture |date=2016 |publisher=Delhi University}}</ref> A. V. Rama Rao Foundation Lecture of Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (2003),<ref name="A.V. Rama Rao Lecture Series">{{Cite web |url=http://www.jncasr.ac.in/blank_page.php/A.V.-Rama-Rao-Lecture-Series/66/1/ |title=A.V. Rama Rao Lecture Series |date=2016 |publisher=Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research}}</ref> Distinguished Lectures and Institute/University colloquia at a number of national institutions including [[Panjab University]] Colloquium of 2016.<ref name="News from Panjab University" /> The Indian Academy of Sciences elected him as a fellow in 1984<ref name="Fellow profile" /> and he became a fellow of the Indian National Science Academy in 1987. He is also an elected part of [[The World Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="TWAS fellow" /> and the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry]].<ref name="Faculty profile" /> In 2019, Deb was conferred a Life-time Achievement Award from the [[Indian Chemical Society]] (estd. 1924) and received this at the Annual Convention of Chemists, Raipur, India.
